- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.5), model underestimates prices; adjust downward bias or add lagged correction.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply mean reversion heuristic: cap forecast at 1.5x prior peak or 20% below recent high.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30d forecasts when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; increase baseline by 2–5% for such cases.
- If sentiment turns negative after a positive spike, model often fails to adjust downward; apply “sentiment reversal” rule: reduce forecast by 3–5% per day of negative sentiment accumulation.
- Model exhibits persistent lag in capturing true price direction after sentiment shifts; add 1–2 day delay in reaction to sentiment changes for price correction.
